verses.jalalayn: ﻿Say: ‘He is God, One (Allāhu is the predicate of huwa, ‘He is’, and ahadun is its substitution or a second predicate).
﻿God, the Self-Sufficient, Besought of all (Allāhu’l-samad constitute a subject and a predicate) [al-samad means] the One Who is always sought at times of need,
verses.romanUrdu: Allah sab se bay-niyaz hai aur sab us kay mohtaj hain

verses.saheeh: He neither begets nor is born,
verses.khattab: He has never had offspring, nor was He born
verses.jalalayn: ﻿He neither begot, for no likeness of Him can exist, nor was begotten, since createdness is precluded in His case.
verses.romanUrdu: Na uski koi aulad hai aur na woh kisi ki aulad

verses.saheeh: Nor is there to Him any equivalent."
verses.khattab: And there is none comparable to Him.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nor is there anyone equal to Him’, neither match nor comparison (lahu, ‘to Him’, is semantically connected to kufuwan, ‘equal’, but precedes it because it is the object of the intended negation; ahadun, ‘anyone’, which is the subject of yakun, ‘is there’, has been placed after the predicate of the latter [kufuwan, ‘equal’] in order to retain the harmony of the end-rhyme [of the verses]).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur koi uska humsar nahin hai
